title: South Korea, AI Basic Act, Article 31, and its Enforcement Decree

sources.title: Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and the Establishment of a Foundation for Trust (인공지능 발전과 신뢰 기반 조성 등에 관한 기본법), consolidated text; Korean text, our translation
Enforcement Decree of the same Act, consolidated text in force 20 August 2026; Korean text, our translation

rules.title: Tell users in advance that the service runs on AI
rules.summary: If Korean users can reach your generative AI product, tell them in advance that it runs on generative AI: in the terms, contract or manual, on the screen, or where the service is provided. This is the Article 31 duty with a direct fine of up to KRW 30 million. The Act applies to businesses abroad whose service affects Korean users.

rules.title: Label generated output, visibly or machine-readably
rules.summary: Indicate that output was generated by generative AI, either in a way a person can perceive or in a way a machine can read; if you choose machine-readable (a signed manifest or a watermark), also tell the user at least once, in text or voice, that the output is AI-generated. Not needed where AI use is obvious from the product or the output.
rules.quote: a method a machine can read
rules.unverified: A law firm reports a one-year grace before fines, to about 22 January 2027; neither the Act nor the Decree contains it and we have not found the Ministry's statement.

rules.title: A clear label on output that could pass as real
rules.summary: Where your system produces sound, images or video that are hard to tell from reality, notify or label it so the user can clearly recognise it as generated. Artistic and creative works may be labelled in a way that does not spoil them.
rules.quote: in a manner the user can clearly recognise
rules.unverified: That only human-perceivable methods count for realistic output comes from a law firm's summary of the Ministry's guidelines, which we have not read.

changelog: 2026.10.13: first version, from /law/south-korea as read 13 October 2026. The domestic-representative duty (Article 36) applies only above revenue or user thresholds and is left out.
